tiers.title: Basic data structures
tiers.description: Learn each structure on its own: structure and operations → applied problems → a DSA connection.

tiers.title: Combined data structures
tiers.description: Combine structures deliberately: model the relationship → handle edge cases → connect it to DSA. A combination is not automatically a harder problem.

tiers.title: Easy to medium DSA
tiers.description: Practice contracts, traces, brute force, invariants, correctness and complexity; build from easy problems to medium ones.

units.title: Arrays
units.objective: Traverse, transform and copy an ordered collection; distinguish index, value and shared references.
units.mental_model: An array is an ordered indexed collection. A new outer array does not automatically copy objects stored inside it.
units.applied_task: Given a list of readings, preserve the original, keep only readings above a threshold, and return their original positions. Handle empty input and equal-to-threshold values.
units.pitfall: Assignment aliases an array; slice/spread copy only one level. Check whether an operation mutates its input.
units.dsa_bridge: Move from a direct scan to a running-best invariant, then compare that approach with nested scans.

activities.title: Trace the structure
activities.prompt: Start with values = [2, 4]. Trace values.push(6), values.pop(), then values[0] = 9. Write the array contents and each expression’s result separately after every step.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Contrast a second case
activities.prompt: Compare [0, false, "", null] filtered by truthiness with a filter that removes only null. Explain which contract each filter satisfies.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Practice the operation
activities.prompt: Implement countAbove for finite numeric readings and a threshold. Count strictly greater values; include empty input and values equal to the threshold.
checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.
Demonstrate an ordinary input and a boundary case.

activities.title: Preserve the contract
activities.prompt: Return a new array with one valid index replaced, leaving the input unchanged. Explain what is and is not copied if an element is itself an object.
checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.
Demonstrate an ordinary input and a boundary case.

activities.title: Handle boundaries
activities.prompt: Specify an index-replacement contract that throws RangeError for non-integer or out-of-range indices. Test -1, length, fractional indices and an empty array.
checklist: Make missing, empty, duplicate and invalid cases explicit where relevant.
Explain why the chosen test distinguishes the required behavior.

activities.title: Make assumptions explicit
activities.prompt: Remove only null entries while retaining 0, false and empty strings in their original order. Explain why the choice of predicate matters.
checklist: Make missing, empty, duplicate and invalid cases explicit where relevant.
Explain why the chosen test distinguishes the required behavior.

activities.title: Solve an applied task
activities.prompt: Find the longest consecutive run of readings strictly above a threshold. Empty input returns 0 and an equal reading breaks the run. Trace [2, 8, 9, 1, 7] with threshold 5.
checklist: Trace a small case before implementing.
State the maintained state and test the failure or reset case.

activities.title: Extend the same structure
activities.prompt: Rotate a dense array right by nonnegative integer k without mutating it. Define empty-input behavior and support k larger than the array length.
checklist: Trace a small case before implementing.
State the maintained state and test the failure or reset case.

activities.title: Diagnose a defect
activities.prompt: A function does const copy = values; copy.push(7), but promises not to change values. Diagnose the violated contract and propose a test that checks the original input.
checklist: Support the diagnosis or choice with a counterexample or trace.
Explain one alternative and its trade-off.

activities.title: Compare approaches
activities.prompt: Compare filter followed by map with one traversal producing the same output. Count inspected elements and intermediate collections; explain a readability trade-off.
checklist: Support the diagnosis or choice with a counterexample or trace.
Explain one alternative and its trade-off.

activities.title: Transfer independently
activities.prompt: Find the second-largest distinct finite number without sorting. Return null if fewer than two distinct numbers exist. Explain your maintained state for duplicates and negative values.
checklist: Try the task before requesting a hint.
Explain why the approach works and check a fresh boundary case.

activities.title: Return for review
activities.prompt: Without notes, revisit ordered readings with a changed contract: return the second-smallest distinct value, or null if absent. Explain how the earlier invariant must change; this is deliberate review.
checklist: Attempt from memory before revisiting the lesson.
Explain how the changed contract affects the earlier approach.

units.title: Strings
units.objective: Read and transform text while stating the character and normalization contract.
units.mental_model: Strings are immutable text values. JavaScript indexing uses UTF-16 code units; for...of iterates code points, which are not always whole user-perceived characters.
units.applied_task: Normalize a small ASCII search phrase: trim it, lowercase it, and count non-space letters without changing the original. Then explain what changes if the contract includes emoji or combining marks.
units.pitfall: Do not assume string length, code-point count and visible character count are the same.
units.dsa_bridge: Use text traversal and frequency counting before combining strings with objects or Map.

activities.title: Trace the structure
activities.prompt: Start with text = "  Cat  ". Trace text.trim().toLowerCase().slice(0, 2), showing the value after each call. State whether the original text changes.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Contrast a second case
activities.prompt: Compare the length and iteration count of a string containing an emoji. Distinguish UTF-16 code units from code points and visible graphemes without treating them as interchangeable.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.
Demonstrate an ordinary input and a boundary case.

activities.title: Preserve the contract

checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.

activities.title: Handle boundaries

units.title: Objects
units.objective: Model a record, distinguish missing properties from falsy values, and reason about shallow copies.
units.mental_model: An object groups named properties. Variables store references to the same object unless you construct a new one.
units.applied_task: Merge a settings patch into a record without mutating the original. Preserve explicit false and 0, reject unexpected keys, and state whether nested records are copied.
units.pitfall: The || fallback replaces valid false/0/empty-string values; ?? only falls back for null or undefined. Shallow copies still share nested objects.
units.dsa_bridge: Use objects for fixed record shapes, then learn when arbitrary-key lookup belongs in a Map.

activities.title: Trace the structure
activities.prompt: Start with record = { points: 0 }, alias = record and copy = { ...record }. Trace alias.points += 1, then copy.points += 2. State each value and which variables refer to the same object.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Contrast a second case
activities.prompt: Compare a missing property with one explicitly set to undefined, and compare || with ??. Explain which observations distinguish absence from a falsy value.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

Demonstrate an ordinary input and a boundary case.

activities.title: Preserve the contract

checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.

activities.title: Handle boundaries

checklist: Make missing, empty, duplicate and invalid cases explicit where relevant.

units.title: Map
units.objective: Choose and use key/value lookup, counting and insertion-order traversal.
units.mental_model: Map stores key/value entries and accepts object keys by identity. It separates entries from ordinary object properties.
units.applied_task: Build a visit counter that updates one key at a time. Explain the absent-key case and why two separately-created object keys do not identify the same entry.
units.pitfall: map[key] accesses an ordinary property; use get/set/has for entries. get returning undefined does not by itself prove a key is absent.
units.dsa_bridge: Use a lookup table to avoid repeatedly scanning for a matching value.

activities.title: Trace the structure
activities.prompt: Start with new Map([["a", 1]]). Trace set("b", 2), set("a", 3), has("b"), delete("b") and get("b"). Distinguish each result, the remaining entries and ordinary object properties.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Contrast a second case
activities.prompt: Use two separately created object keys with equal fields. Predict which lookups succeed, then contrast object identity with using a stable string identifier.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Practice the operation
activities.prompt: Count visits per ASCII page key using Map. Start absent keys at zero, preserve existing counts and test an empty input.
checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.
Demonstrate an ordinary input and a boundary case.

activities.title: Preserve the contract
activities.prompt: Merge two numeric counters under an explicit sum-on-duplicate policy without mutating either input Map. State the output’s iteration order.
checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.

activities.title: Handle boundaries

activities.title: Make assumptions explicit

units.title: Set
units.objective: Model uniqueness and membership while preserving a clear equality contract.
units.mental_model: Set holds unique values. Objects are compared by identity; two separate records with equal fields are still different values.

structure.code:
const tags = new Set(["js", "js", "web"]);
console.log(JSON.stringify([tags.size, tags.has("web"), [...tags]]));

units.applied_task: Return the first occurrence of each identifier while preserving input order. Handle empty input and explain why record deduplication needs an explicit key.
units.pitfall: A Set of objects does not deduplicate by an id field automatically.
units.dsa_bridge: Use a seen-values invariant to detect duplicates in one traversal.

activities.title: Trace the structure
activities.prompt: Start with new Set(["a"]). Trace add("a"), add("b"), has("b") and delete("a"), writing the members and size after each operation.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Contrast a second case
activities.prompt: Predict the size of a Set containing two separate objects with identical id fields. Explain identity versus deduplication by a chosen field.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.

activities.title: Preserve the contract

checklist: State inputs, outputs and the mutation contract.

checklist: Make missing, empty, duplicate and invalid cases explicit where relevant.

checklist: Support the diagnosis or choice with a counterexample or trace.

activities.title: Return for review

checklist: Attempt from memory before revisiting the lesson.
Explain how the changed contract affects the earlier approach.

units.title: Stacks
units.objective: Model last-in, first-out operations and an explicit empty-stack contract.
units.mental_model: A stack exposes one end: the most recently pushed item is the next one popped.
units.applied_task: Model undo/redo using two stacks. Explain how a new edit changes the redo history and what undo does when no edit remains.
units.pitfall: Do not confuse stack top with the oldest element; define behavior for an empty pop.
units.dsa_bridge: Apply the stack invariant to nested delimiters and iterative traversal; dedicated graded stack questions are still to be authored.

activities.title: Trace the structure
activities.prompt: Starting from an empty array-backed stack, trace push("a"), push("b"), pop(), pop() and pop(). State the top, result and remaining contents after each operation, including the empty pop.
checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.
Explain the rule behind the first surprising result.

activities.title: Contrast a second case

units.title: Queues
units.objective: Model first-in, first-out processing without accidentally processing a new task first.
units.mental_model: A queue serves the oldest pending entry. A head index can advance without shifting every stored element.
units.applied_task: Simulate a service queue: add requests, serve the oldest, and report pending requests. Define the empty case and when consumed storage should be reclaimed.
units.pitfall: A head-index queue still retains consumed storage until compacted or replaced; do not claim it uses bounded memory without cleanup.
units.dsa_bridge: Use FIFO order for breadth-first exploration; graded queue/BFS exercises are a later content addition.

units.title: Linked lists
units.objective: Trace nodes and next references, preserve the remaining chain, and handle a missing head.
units.mental_model: A linked list is a chain of separate nodes. A reference identifies a node; changing next rewires the chain.
units.applied_task: Draw and trace removal of one node from a three-node chain. Explain the head-removal, single-node and empty-list cases before writing code.
units.pitfall: Overwriting the only reference to the remaining chain can make nodes unreachable.
units.dsa_bridge: Keep a precise reference invariant while reversing a list.

checklist: Show the state or output at each relevant step.

units.title: Medium DSA: sorting and two pointers
units.objective: Justify each pointer movement and distinguish mutation costs from search costs.
units.mental_model: Two pointers are useful only when the contract or ordering gives a reason to eliminate candidates safely.
units.applied_task: Explain which candidates a pointer movement rules out. Include duplicates and small inputs, and account for sorting in the total cost.
units.pitfall: The default array sort compares string forms; sorting with a comparator still requires a clear mutation contract.
units.dsa_bridge: These medium problems require different elimination arguments; do not apply one pointer rule blindly.

units.title: Medium DSA: prefix and suffix state
units.objective: Use information from both sides of an element without accidentally depending on an overwritten value.
units.mental_model: A prefix summarizes items before a position; a suffix summarizes items after it. State exactly which positions are included.
units.applied_task: Draw the auxiliary state for a small array, including a zero. Separate the reference implementation from a space-optimized variant.
units.pitfall: Off-by-one boundaries and zero handling can invalidate an otherwise convincing aggregate formula.
units.dsa_bridge: Use independent prefix/suffix summaries for the linked medium exercise.

units.title: Easy to medium DSA: state and recurrence
units.objective: Define a state, base cases and a dependency order before implementing a recurrence.
units.mental_model: Dynamic programming reuses results of well-defined smaller subproblems; a recurrence without a precise state is not yet an algorithm.
units.applied_task: First describe the state in one sentence and enumerate small cases manually. For minimum-count tasks, distinguish unreachable from a valid zero count.
units.pitfall: A recurrence can count ordered sequences instead of combinations, or mishandle unreachable states, unless the contract is explicit.
units.dsa_bridge: Start with a small recurrence, then move to a medium minimum-count problem.
